cases.explain: «В» with a verb of motion (уезжают — going away to a place) takes the accusative; Харьков is inanimate, so its accusative is identical to the nominative.

cases.translation: I hid it in the cellar!
cases.explain: «В» meaning location (where something is, not motion towards) takes the prepositional case.

cases.sentence: С ___ все ходит, Ивана Петровича ищет.
cases.translation: She keeps walking about with the doctor, looking for Ivan Petrovich.
cases.explain: The preposition «с» in the sense of accompaniment («together with») always governs the instrumental.

cases.sentence: На стене карта ___, видимо, никому здесь не нужная.
cases.translation: On the wall there is a map of Africa, evidently of no use to anyone here.
cases.explain: A noun depending on another noun and meaning «of X» (a map of Africa) stands in the genitive.

cases.sentence: Я покушался на ___, а меня не арестовывают, не отдают под суд.
cases.translation: I attempted murder, and they do not arrest me, do not put me on trial.
cases.explain: «Покушаться на» (to make an attempt on something) requires «на» + accusative; the neuter noun убийство looks the same as the nominative.

cases.sentence: Ты взял у меня из дорожной аптеки баночку с ___.
cases.translation: You took a little jar of morphine from my travelling medicine case.
cases.explain: «С» describing the contents of a container («a jar with morphine in it») takes the instrumental.

cases.translation: The horses have already been brought round.
cases.explain: The horses are the subject of the passive predicate «поданы», so the noun stands in the nominative plural.

cases.sentence: Идите к ___, он хочет что-то сказать вам.
cases.translation: Go to Alexander, he wants to say something to you.
cases.explain: The preposition «к» (towards, to a person) always governs the dative.

cases.sentence: Давно уже я, грешница, ___ не ела.
cases.translation: It's a long time since I, sinner that I am, have eaten noodles.
cases.explain: The object of a negated verb («не ела») normally goes into the genitive, especially with mass nouns like лапша.

cases.sentence: Мы услышим ангелов, мы увидим все небо в ___.
cases.translation: We shall hear the angels, we shall see the whole sky in diamonds.
cases.explain: «В» describing a state or covering (the sky decked in diamonds), with no motion involved, takes the prepositional.

reading.ru: Телегин и Марина сидят друг против друга и мотают чулочную шерсть.
reading.question: What are Telegin and Marina doing when Act Four opens?
options: Sitting opposite each other winding stocking wool
reading.correct: Sitting opposite each other winding stocking wool
reading.explain: The opening stage direction shows them facing each other and winding wool for stockings.

reading.ru: В Харьков уезжают.
reading.question: Where are Serebryakov and Elena going to live?
reading.correct: Kharkov
reading.explain: Telegin tells Marina they are leaving for Kharkov and will live there.

reading.ru: Я в погребе спрятал!
reading.question: Where did Telegin hide Voynitsky's pistol?
reading.correct: In the cellar
reading.explain: Telegin whispers to Marina that he hid the pistol in the cellar.

reading.ru: Боятся, как бы он на себя рук не наложил.
reading.question: Why are Sonya and the doctor walking about the garden looking for Ivan Petrovich?
options: They are afraid he will lay hands on himself
They want him to say goodbye to the professor
They need him to sign the accounts
They are looking for the missing horses
reading.correct: They are afraid he will lay hands on himself
reading.explain: Telegin says they fear Voynitsky will kill himself.

reading.ru: Все мы у бога приживалы.
reading.question: How does Marina console Telegin after a shopkeeper called him a sponger?
options: She says that before God we are all hangers-on and all of us work
She says the shopkeeper is a drunkard whose words mean nothing
She promises to complain to Ivan Petrovich about him
She tells him to move away to Kharkov with the professor
reading.correct: She says that before God we are all hangers-on and all of us work
reading.explain: Marina answers that everyone — he, Sonya, Ivan Petrovich — is a hanger-on before God and nobody sits idle.

reading.ru: Уйдите отсюда, оставьте меня одного хоть на один час!
reading.question: What does Voynitsky demand of Marina and Telegin when he comes in from the yard?
options: That they go away and leave him alone for at least an hour
That they help him find his pistol
That they bring him tea and vodka
That they fetch the professor to him
reading.correct: That they go away and leave him alone for at least an hour
reading.explain: He drives them out, saying he cannot bear being watched over.

reading.ru: Я у тебя ничего не брал.
reading.question: What does Voynitsky keep repeating when Astrov demands his property back?
options: That he took nothing from him
That he will return it tomorrow
That he threw it into the pond
reading.correct: That he took nothing from him
reading.explain: Voynitsky denies the theft several times before finally handing the jar over.

reading.ru: Свяжем тебя и обыщем.
reading.question: What does Astrov threaten to do if Voynitsky will not give the thing back?
options: Tie him up and search him
reading.correct: Tie him up and search him
reading.explain: Astrov says quite seriously that he will resort to force, tie him up and search him.

reading.ru: Этого я себе никогда не прощу!
reading.question: What can Voynitsky never forgive himself for?
options: Making a fool of himself by firing twice and missing both times
Letting Elena leave without saying goodbye
Signing the estate over to the professor
reading.correct: Making a fool of himself by firing twice and missing both times
reading.explain: He says he played the fool: he shot twice and did not hit once.

reading.ru: Ты не сумасшедший, а просто чудак.
reading.question: How does Astrov classify Voynitsky?
options: Not a madman, just a crank
A genuinely sick man who needs a hospital
reading.correct: Not a madman, just a crank
reading.explain: Astrov says being a crank is in fact the normal condition of a human being.

reading.ru: Мне сорок семь лет; если, положим, я проживу до шестидесяти, то мне остается еще тринадцать.
reading.question: How old is Voynitsky, and how many years does he reckon he has left?
reading.correct: Forty-seven, with thirteen years left
reading.explain: He counts from forty-seven to a supposed sixty and asks how he will fill those thirteen years.

reading.ru: Наше положение, твое и мое, безнадежно.
reading.question: What is Astrov's verdict on the position he and Voynitsky are in?
options: It will improve once the professor leaves
It is no worse than anyone else's
It can be mended by hard work
reading.correct: It is hopeless
reading.explain: Astrov brushes aside the idea of a new life and says he is convinced their position is hopeless.

reading.ru: Ты взял у меня из дорожной аптеки баночку с морфием.
reading.question: What exactly did Voynitsky take from Astrov?
options: A little jar of morphine from his travelling medicine case
A revolver from his coat pocket
A folder of his estate maps
A bottle of vodka from his trunk
reading.correct: A little jar of morphine from his travelling medicine case
reading.explain: Astrov names the stolen item after Voynitsky's repeated denials.

reading.ru: Морфий же отдай, а то пойдут разговоры, догадки, подумают, что это я тебе дал...
reading.question: What reason does Astrov give for wanting the morphine back?
options: People will gossip and suspect that he supplied it
He needs it for a patient in the village
It is the last jar he owns
Sonya asked him to take it away
reading.correct: People will gossip and suspect that he supplied it
reading.explain: He adds that it would be quite enough for him to have to perform the autopsy.

reading.ru: Я терплю и буду терпеть, пока жизнь моя не окончится сама собою...
reading.question: What does Sonya say about her own unhappiness while begging for the jar?
options: She endures and will go on enduring instead of despairing
She is happier now that the professor is leaving
She will follow her uncle if he does it
reading.correct: She endures and will go on enduring instead of despairing
reading.explain: She says she may be no less unhappy than he is, yet does not fall into despair.

reading.ru: Папа и ты должны помириться.
reading.question: Why does Sonya take her uncle by the arm and lead him out?
options: Because he and her father must be reconciled
Because the horses are waiting for him
Because the doctor wants to examine him
Because he must sign the accounts
reading.correct: Because he and her father must be reconciled
reading.explain: Elena says Alexander wants to tell him something, and Sonya calls the reconciliation necessary.

reading.ru: Этот карандаш я беру себе на память.
reading.question: What does Elena quietly take from Astrov's table as a keepsake?
reading.correct: A pencil
reading.explain: She picks the pencil off his table and hides it quickly.

reading.ru: Я даже увлеклась вами немножко.
reading.question: What does Elena admit to Astrov at their parting?
options: That she was a little carried away by him
That she never liked him at all
That she intends to write to him from Kharkov
That she told her husband everything
reading.correct: That she was a little carried away by him
reading.explain: She says there is no point hiding it since they will never meet again, and proposes they part as friends.

reading.ru: Итак, куда бы ни ступили вы и ваш муж, всюду вы вносите разрушение...
reading.question: What does Astrov accuse Elena and her husband of doing?
options: Bringing destruction wherever they set foot
Spreading gossip about him in the district
reading.correct: Bringing destruction wherever they set foot
reading.explain: He says their idleness infected everyone and that he himself did nothing for a whole month.

reading.ru: Надо дело делать!
reading.question: What is Serebryakov's parting piece of advice to the household?
options: One must work, one must get things done
One must live in a town, not the country
One must not think about the future
reading.correct: One must work, one must get things done
reading.explain: He allows himself this one remark in his farewell greeting to Astrov and the others.

reading.ru: Александр, снимитесь опять и пришлите мне вашу фотографию.
reading.question: What does Maria Vasilyevna ask Serebryakov for as he leaves?
options: To have a new photograph taken and send it to her
To write her a treatise on how to live
To take her with him to Kharkov
reading.correct: To have a new photograph taken and send it to her
reading.explain: She kisses him and tells him how dear he is to her.

reading.ru: Ты будешь аккуратно получать то же, что получал и раньше.
reading.question: What does Voynitsky promise Serebryakov after their reconciliation?
options: That he will receive the same payments as before, punctually
That he will never write to him again
That he will sell the estate for him
That he will come to Kharkov in the spring
reading.correct: That he will receive the same payments as before, punctually
reading.explain: Voynitsky says everything will go on in the old way.

reading.ru: Моя пристяжная что-то захромала.
reading.question: What does Astrov mention about his horses before he drives off?
options: One of the trace-horses has gone lame
They have not been fed since morning
They were sent back to Rozhdestvennoye
reading.correct: One of the trace-horses has gone lame
reading.explain: He says he will have to call at the blacksmith's in Rozhdestvennoye.

reading.ru: Может, водочки выпьешь?
reading.question: What does Marina offer Astrov after he refuses to stay for tea?
options: A slice of bread and honey
reading.correct: A drop of vodka
reading.explain: He hesitantly agrees, and she brings a glass of vodka and a piece of bread on a tray.

reading.ru: Что же делать, надо жить!
reading.question: How does Sonya answer her uncle's cry that life is unbearably hard for him?
options: There is nothing to be done, one must live
He should go away with the professor
She will fetch the doctor back
He should take the morphine after all
reading.correct: There is nothing to be done, one must live
reading.explain: Her answer opens the long closing speech about working on and finding rest.

reading.ru: Мы отдохнем!
reading.question: What phrase does Sonya repeat again and again as the curtain falls?
reading.correct: «We shall rest!»
reading.explain: The words «Мы отдохнем!» close the play, over Telegin's quiet guitar.

highlight.question: Which sentence tells you what hangs on the wall of Ivan Petrovich's room?
sentences: Комната Ивана Петровича; тут его спальня, тут же и контора имения.
У окна большой стол с приходо-расходными книгами и бумагами всякого рода, конторка, шкафы, весы.
Стол поменьше для Астрова; на этом столе принадлежности для рисования, краски; возле папка.
Клетка со скворцом.
На стене карта Африки, видимо, никому здесь не нужная.
Громадный диван, обитый клеенкой.
Налево - дверь, ведущая в покои; направо - дверь в сени; подле правой двери положен половик, чтобы не нагрязнили мужики.
Осенний вечер.
highlight.explain: Only this sentence names the map of Africa hanging on the wall that nobody there needs.

highlight.question: Which sentence sets out the hours of the household's ordinary day?
sentences: Опять заживем, как было, по-старому.
Утром в восьмом часу чай, в первом часу обед, вечером - ужинать садиться; все своим порядком, как у людей... по-христиански.
Давно уже я, грешница, лапши не ела.
Да, давненько у нас лапши не готовили.
highlight.explain: Only the second sentence lists the times of tea, dinner and supper.

highlight.question: Which sentence states Voynitsky's age and how many years he expects to have left?
sentences: Дай мне чего-нибудь.
О боже мой...
Мне сорок семь лет; если, положим, я проживу до шестидесяти, то мне остается еще тринадцать.
Долго!
Как я проживу эти тринадцать лет?
Что буду делать, чем наполню их?
highlight.explain: The third sentence gives both the age forty-seven and the thirteen remaining years.

highlight.question: Which sentence says how many decent, educated people there were in the whole district?
sentences: Да, брат.
Во всем уезде было только два порядочных, интеллигентных человека: я да ты.
Но в какие-нибудь десять лет жизнь обывательская, жизнь презренная затянула нас; она своими гнилыми испарениями травила нашу кровь, и мы стали такими же пошляками, как все.
Но ты мне зубов не заговаривай, однако.
Ты отдай то, что взял у меня.
highlight.explain: Astrov counts exactly two such people in the district — himself and Voynitsky.

highlight.question: Which sentence gives Astrov's reason for insisting the morphine be handed back?
sentences: Послушай, если тебе во что бы то ни стало хочется покончить с собою, то ступай в лес и застрелись там.
Морфий же отдай, а то пойдут разговоры, догадки, подумают, что это я тебе дал...
С меня же довольно и того, что мне придется вскрывать тебя...
Ты думаешь, это интересно?
highlight.explain: Only this sentence explains that people would gossip and suspect Astrov of supplying the drug.

highlight.question: Which sentence compares Sonya's own unhappiness with her uncle's?
sentences: Отдай.
Зачем ты нас пугаешь?
Отдай, дядя Ваня!
Я, быть может, несчастна не меньше твоего, однако же не прихожу в отчаяние.
Я терплю и буду терпеть, пока жизнь моя не окончится сама собою...
Терпи и ты.
highlight.explain: Sonya says she is perhaps no less unhappy than he is, yet does not give way to despair.

highlight.question: Which sentence has Serebryakov claim he could write a whole treatise on how one should live?
sentences: Кто старое помянет, тому глаз вон.
После того, что случилось, в эти несколько часов я так много пережил и столько передумал, что, кажется, мог бы написать в назидание потомству целый трактат о том, как надо жить.
Я охотно принимаю твои извинения и сам прошу извинить меня.
Прощай!
highlight.explain: The second sentence is where he boasts of the treatise he could write for posterity.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes what they will see in the sky?
sentences: Мы отдохнем!

Мы услышим ангелов, мы увидим все небо в алмазах, мы увидим, как все зло земное, все наши страдания потонут в милосердии, которое наполнит собою весь мир, и наша жизнь станет тихою, нежною, сладкою, как ласка.
Я верую, верую...
Бедный, бедный дядя Ваня, ты плачешь...
Ты не знал в своей жизни радостей, но погоди, дядя Ваня, погоди...
Мы отдохнем...
highlight.explain: Only this sentence mentions the whole sky seen in diamonds.
